author: israellot
body:
## Summary

DeltaSharp parses delta blobs that may be **attacker-controlled**. A multi-agent bug scan of the read path found several spots where a length/position taken from the delta was used to slice or dereference a span without being fully validated. On a crafted delta these threw a raw `IndexOutOfRangeException` / `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` (DoS-shaped — wrong, untyped exception escaping the `TryRead`/`Apply` contract) or, in one case, silently overflowed and produced corrupt output. Spans are bounds-checked so none are raw memory-unsafety **except `DecodeUnsafe`**, which over-read a short buffer; all violate the documented "return `false` / throw a typed exception" contract on bad input.

## Fixes

| Path | Defect | Fix |
|------|--------|-----|
| `DeltaApply` COPY | only `Position` checked against source, not `Position + Length` → `source.Slice` reads past end | add `Position + Length > source.Length` check (in `ulong` space, so the sum can't 32-bit-overflow past the guard) |
| `DeltaApply` INSERT | declared length checked against output span only, not the remaining delta → `delta.Slice` overruns | add `Length > delta.Length` check on the delta tail |
| `FossilDeltaReader.TryRead` | `input[0]` read after `ReadInt` with no empty-check → all-digit / no-command delta throws `IndexOutOfRangeException` | guard `input.IsEmpty` → return `false` |
| `FossilDeltaReader.ReadInt` | 6-bit-per-digit accumulator silently overflows 32 bits on a long digit run → corrupt length/offset | reject when the top 6 bits are already set (typed `DeltaReaderException`) |
| `ASCIIDeltaReader.TryRead` | line-break skip loop derefs `input[0]` with no re-check → all-`\n`/`\r` input throws `IndexOutOfRangeException` | re-check `IsEmpty` inside and after the loop |
| `ASCIIDeltaReader` COPY | `Slice(positionBytes+1)` assumes a separator byte without validating it | require a `' '` separator between the position and length numbers |
| `DeltaApplyException(error)` | constructor never assigned `Error` → every apply error reported the default (`InvalidDelta`) | assign `Error = error` |
| `VarIntFormatter.DecodeUnsafe` | multi-byte lead bytes (241-255) read `buffer[1..8]` with no length check → **OOB read** past a truncated buffer | bounds-check every multi-byte case; on a short buffer return `consumed = 0` (the existing "could-not-decode" sentinel) instead of over-reading |

## Tests

Adds `MalformedInputHardeningTests` — one crafted malformed input per path, asserting a clean failure (`TryRead == false`, a typed `DeltaReaderException` / `DeltaApplyException`, or `consumed == 0`), plus round-trip sanity checks so the new guards aren't too eager. Full suite **51/51** (41 pre-existing + 10 new). Build clean.

### Note on `DecodeUnsafe`
It keeps its non-throwing `*Unsafe` fast-path contract (mirrors `EncodeUnsafe`): the caller is still expected to supply a large-enough buffer, but a short/truncated buffer now signals failure via `consumed = 0` rather than reading out of bounds. It has no parse-path caller today (the binary reader uses the safe `TryDecode`), but it is public API, so the guard closes a latent OOB. **Callers must check `consumed != 0`.**

body:
## Summary

Renders fenced ```mermaid``` blocks as diagrams in the markdown renderer — the same renderer used by published articles and chat sessions — mirroring the existing Vega-Lite `chart` support. A diagram leads with a Diagram/Source tab toggle and an enlarge-to-modal action, and the session system prompt now tells the model it can emit them.

## GitHub Issue

N/A

## What Changed

- **Mermaid rendering.** `Pre` in the markdown component routes a ```mermaid``` fence to a new lazy `Mermaid` component, exactly as ```chart``` routes to the lazy chart renderer. mermaid is code-split into its own chunk (~140 kB gzip), so documents without a diagram pay nothing. Diagrams are themed from the design tokens (like the chart renderer) and a malformed/hostile diagram degrades to an inline notice rather than breaking the surrounding document.
- **Diagram / Source tabs + enlarge.** The diagram leads; a Source tab exposes the raw mermaid text with a copy action (positioned top-right). An Enlarge action opens the diagram in a viewport-spanning modal so large graphs get room.
- **Two design-system primitive additions** that the feature needed: `Tabs` gains an opt-in `local` (uncontrolled) mode so an inline, repeatable widget doesn't fight over the URL search param; `Modal` gains a `full` size that spans most of the viewport. Both carry catalogue entries and tests.
- **Session system prompt.** The kiri core layer now advertises ```mermaid``` diagrams alongside the chart guidance, with the same shape (when to use, mechanics, worked example) and a structure-vs-quantities distinction so the model doesn't over-reach.
- **Docs swept**: the security invariant in `design-notes.md`, the `publish:` description, the README, the workflow-authoring reference, and the living design-system catalogue.

## Notes for Reviewers

- **Security carve-out.** mermaid is a string→SVG renderer, so the SVG is embedded inline via `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`. It runs in `securityLevel: 'strict'`, whose DOMPurify pass strips scripts/handlers before the markup is returned. The `design-notes.md` invariant — previously a blanket "never `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`" — is updated to record this as the single sanitiser-gated exception. Worth a careful look since article/session content is untrusted.
- **No Playwright e2e.** Unit tests mock mermaid (it can't lay out SVG under happy-dom, same as charts); a real render is best exercised by an e2e mirroring `published-charts.spec.ts` if we want it as a follow-up.
- The mermaid library is large (~592 kB raw); lazy-loading contains it. Slimming via a custom build is a possible later optimisation.

Coverage stays at 100%; typecheck, lint, and the production build are green.

body:
## Summary

Migrates the tester from deAPI **API v1 → v2**, builds substantial new capability on top (real-time WebSocket job tracking, prompt booster), and hardens the repository for **public release**.

## API v2 migration
- All endpoints/calls moved to API v2 (`https://api.deapi.ai/api/v2`): job status via `/jobs/{id}`, failures via `error_message`/`error_code`, balance via `/account/balance`.
- **Result display fixed** — media type detected from the result-URL extension + endpoint group (`job.endpointId` stores the v2 path); inline image/video/audio previews with Open/Download.
- **Price calculation fixed** across endpoints — multipart price requests now mirror the main request with the real files (no more `422`).

## Prompt booster (prompt enhancement)
- Unified `POST /prompts/enhancements` (multipart, synchronous). Standalone **Prompt Booster** endpoint **and** an in-form **Boost** button next to prompt/caption fields. Each boost is logged as a job with its cost; `model_slug` is filtered by the selected inference type.

## Real-time WebSocket tracking (primary) + polling fallback
- WebSocket (Pusher-compatible **soketi**) is now the **primary** status source — live status, progress, and image previews. HTTP **polling is an automatic fallback** (configurable interval, default 10s) that also surfaces failures, which deAPI delivers via webhooks (never over the socket).
- **Per-profile WS config auto-fills per environment** (production / dev / sandbox presets); to enable, a profile needs only its **API token** + a **Client ID** from the dashboard. Without a Client ID it transparently runs on polling.
- New: `POST /api/ws-auth` (token-injecting private-channel auth proxy — token stays server-side), `GET /api/jobs/[id]` (one-shot status fetch + persist), `JobSocketContext` (pusher-js, SSR-safe), and a **WS status indicator** in the header (left of balance).
- `WS`/`POLL` source labels on every update; the on-`done` finalize persists cost/result silently; polling is skipped while the socket is actively driving a job.

## UX
- **Show response headers** setting (response HTTP headers in each job's Raw panel).
- **Copy** button for text outputs (OCR / prompt booster), with an icon distinct from Duplicate.
- Bottom spacer so the floating dev indicator no longer overlaps the endpoint list.

## Public-release prep
- **Secret audit: clean** — no API tokens are tracked or present anywhere in git history; `config.example.json` / `.env.local.example` are placeholders only.
- Default profile renamed **Production** — a ready-to-use production profile ships out of the box; the user only adds their token. `data/config.json` is created on first save and is never committed.
- `data/config.example.json` updated to the current multi-profile + WS schema; `.gitignore` hardened; **README** documents WebSockets, the production profile, config-on-save, and all env vars (incl. `DEAPI_FALLBACK_POLLING_INTERVAL_MS`).
- Removed dead SSE code superseded by the WebSocket rewrite: `api/poll/[id]`, `JobTracker.tsx`, `usePolling.ts`.

## Verification
- `npm run build` ✓ and `npm run lint` ✓.
- Multi-agent secret-leak audit across tracked files + full git history → **SAFE to go public**.

author: dmgiulioromano
body:
## Summary

Fixes visual artifacts where tick labels overlap when colorbars and waveform axes are stacked with zero spacing (`hspace=0`, `wspace=0`). When multiple axes share borders, their extreme tick labels (e.g., top tick of lower colorbar and bottom tick of upper colorbar) fall on the same edge and render on top of each other, creating illegible merged text like "3030".

## Key Changes

- **Colorbar tick filtering** (`_add_pitch_colorbar`): Filter out ticks within 4% of the colorbar range extremes, keeping only interior ticks. This prevents the top and bottom ticks from appearing on shared borders between stacked colorbars.

- **Waveform axis tick filtering** (`render_page`): Apply the same 4% margin filtering to Y-axis ticks of the waveform ruler. Explicitly set `ylim` after `set_yticks()` to prevent matplotlib from auto-expanding the limits.

- **Grid spacing adjustment**: Change `wspace` from `0.02` to `0.0` to eliminate the vertical gap between columns, aligning the waveform ruler flush against the grain canvas and the pitch colorbar flush against the right edge.

- **Breakpoint label positioning** (`_annotate_breakpoints`): Replace fixed offset `(3, 3)` with dynamic positioning logic that keeps labels inside the envelope subplot:
  - Horizontal: labels appear left of the point if `x_frac > 0.85` (near right edge), otherwise right
  - Vertical: labels appear below the point if `y_frac > 0.9` (near top), otherwise above
  - Uses `ha` and `va` parameters to control text alignment relative to the offset point

## Implementation Details

- Tick filtering uses a consistent 4% margin formula: `norm.vmin + 0.04 * span < t < norm.vmax - 0.04 * span`
- Waveform Y-axis limits are set with a small padding (`±0.02 s`) to provide visual breathing room while filtering interior ticks
- Breakpoint label positioning is computed as a fraction of the subplot's visible range, making it robust to different time windows and envelope scales
- All changes preserve backward compatibility; no API modifications

body:
### Motivation
- Prevent generated sea areas created during coastal region generation from introducing isolated sea tiles that are not connected to the sea hex adjacent to the river mouth. 
- Avoid creating one-off sea pockets that break river/sea validation and later region generation attempts. 
- When a newly-created sea area contains tiles that do not form a single connected component with the first sea hex touching the river mouth, those tiles should be demoted back to candidate hexes instead of being written as `sea` terrain.

### Description
- Added `splitNewSeaKeysByMouthConnectedComponent(newSeaKeys, rivers)` to split newly created sea keys into the connected component containing the mouth-touching sea hex and the disconnected keys. 
- Added `addCandidateHexKeys(candidateHexes, keysToAdd, blockedKeys)` helper to safely reintroduce demoted sea keys into `candidateHexes` without duplicates and while respecting blocked/occupied keys. 
- Updated the coastal finalization logic in `src/App.tsx` to: filter the generated sea set with the connected-component result, remove demoted keys from pocket fill sets, and re-add demoted keys into the candidate list while preventing collisions with existing land/sea. 
- Adjusted the final sea validation path to use the actually kept sea keys (connected to the mouth) when checking for river/sea height and connectivity violations.

body:
## Summary
- Switches `tools/sprite_gen` to `gemini-3-pro-image` ("Nano Banana Pro").
- Rebuilds the Player sprite generator around per-animation **strips**: one Gemini call produces an entire multi-frame animation (down/up/side) on a fixed magenta background, instead of one call per static frame, so frames within an animation stay visually consistent.
- New post-processing chain (`strips.py`): samples each strip's actual rendered background color from its own border/frequency analysis and keys it out, trims any letterbox margin/gutter Gemini occasionally pads a strip with, computes one scale factor per strip from the median cell silhouette height (with a calibration round-trip to correct for Lanczos edge-softening at this pipeline's extreme downscale ratios), Lanczos-downscales, snaps every pixel to a locked 20-color palette (`palette.json`/`palette.py`), despeckles, and re-centers on a fixed 48x64 canvas with a consistent baseline.
- New automated QA (`qa.py`): checks canvas size, zero off-palette pixels, zero key-color fringe, baseline/height tolerance, and a bbox fill-ratio check that catches an unkeyed background surviving as a solid opaque block.
- New `gif.py` for sheet/GIF preview generation, written to gitignored `tools/sprite_gen/qa_sheets/`.
- New CLI subcommands in `generate_sprites.py`: `turnaround` / `approve-turnaround` / `strip` (`--canary`/`--all`/`--only`) / `reprocess` (re-runs post-processing on already-generated raw strips with no new API calls, e.g. for pipeline bug fixes).
- Deletes the superseded single-frame `postprocess.py`.
- Includes the approved master turnaround reference (`tools/sprite_gen/reference/turnaround.png`, AI-generated, no personal data) and all 45 regenerated Player animation strips, sliced into their final frames in `assets/sprites/player/processed/`.
- New `update_player_tscn.py`: rewires `Player.tscn`'s texture resources and `SpriteFrames` to the new multi-frame strips, and retunes the Player/Hitbox/Hurtbox collision shapes for the new 48x64 cell size.

### Bugs found and fixed during canary review (background keying, identity drift)
The first `idle_down` strip's rendered "magenta" background drifted far enough from pure `#FF00FF` to dodge a fixed-magenta keying threshold but close enough to a real palette skin tone to get palette-snapped into a solid opaque block. Fixed by sampling the strip's own border as the key color per-generation, plus a fill-ratio QA check as defense in depth. A second bug (contradictory hair-shape instructions in the style-lock prompt) caused `idle_down`'s camera angle/hairstyle to drift from the approved turnaround; fixed by rewriting the instruction to treat the turnaround image as unambiguous ground truth.

### Bugs found and fixed during the full 45-strip rollout
The Phase 3 batch came back with 3 hard failures and 8 strips rendering well under their target height. Both turned out to be pipeline bugs, not generation defects:
- **Letterbox margin/gutter false floor**: `trim_letterbox_margin` re-derived a looser RGB-distance check against the key color to find Gemini's occasional white/black letterbox padding. That looser threshold let a thin antialiased seam between the margin and the true background survive as opaque, inflating the raw silhouette height used for per-strip scale calibration. Fixed by scanning the cell's own already-hardened alpha channel directly instead of re-deriving a separate color check.
- **Lanczos downscale edge softening**: raw cells are >1000px tall and get downscaled ~20x to a ~50px target; Lanczos softens the silhouette edges more at that ratio than the pre-resize bbox measurement accounts for, so re-hardening at a fixed alpha threshold trimmed off more height than intended. Fixed with a one-pass calibration round-trip: render once, measure the actual achieved height, correct the scale, render again.

Both fixes resolved all 11 flagged strips at zero additional API cost (re-ran via `reprocess`, no new Gemini calls). The 2 remaining edge-of-tolerance QA flags are confirmed-legitimate per-frame pose variance (a forward lean, a crouch wind-up), and one fill-ratio flag is a false positive for an inherently blocky kick silhouette — all visually verified clean via spot-checks across punch/kick/master/hurt/release/charge_loop families and all 3 directions.

### Godot integration (`Player.tscn`)
`update_player_tscn.py` regenerates the texture `ext_resource` block and the `SpriteFrames` sub-resource from `poses.py`'s frame counts and the on-disk strip-sliced PNGs, replacing the 45 old single-frame textures with the full per-animation frame sequences (4 frames for looping idle/move/charge_loop, 3 for everything else). Looping animations play at a fixed 6.0 visual cadence; bounded attacks keep their existing `AnimationPlayer` gameplay length (`speed = frame_count / length`: 25.0 for the 0.12s punch/kick/master hits, 7.5 for the 0.4s hurt flinch); `release` has no `AnimationPlayer` coupling so its speed (8.0) is a visual judgement call. Everything else in the scene — scripts, the combat-timing `Animation`/`AnimationLibrary` resources, the node tree — is untouched. The 45 superseded single-frame PNGs are deleted.

Collision shapes are retuned for the new 48x64 cell (height ratio 52/56, approximate starting values): `CapsuleShape2D_body` radius 8.0→7.5, height 28.0→26.0; `Hitbox`'s `RectangleShape2D` 20x16→19x15 and `reach` 14.0→13.0; `Hurtbox`'s `RectangleShape2D` 16x28→15x26. Boss is untouched (placeholder sprites, independently-sized capsule).

## Test plan
- [x] `python3 -m py_compile` on all `tools/sprite_gen/*.py`
- [x] Validated the full post-processing chain on a synthetic magenta-background test strip
- [x] Generated and visually approved the master turnaround (down/up/side) against the perspective/identity checklist
- [x] Generated both canary strips (`idle_down`, `move_side`), diagnosed and fixed two pipeline bugs, confirmed clean output
- [x] Ran the full 43-strip Phase 3 rollout, diagnosed and fixed two further pipeline bugs (letterbox-margin seam, Lanczos edge softening) at zero added API cost, reprocessed all 45 strips
- [x] Spot-checked representative frames across every pose family (punch, kick, master hit, hurt, release, charge loop) and all 3 directions for identity/scale/baseline consistency
- [x] Rewired `Player.tscn` to the new strip-sliced frames and retuned collision shapes for the new 48x64 cell size; verified all 144 referenced textures exist on disk and the scene's brace/bracket structure stays balanced
- [ ] Manual verification in the Godot editor (no `godot` binary in this sandbox): confirm the scene parses, play idle/move/attack/hurt in all directions, and re-tune the collision sizes by eye against real gameplay feel — the values above are a reasoned starting point, not a final tuning pass

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary

The app had no error handling — any failure in Snowflake connections, Cortex search, or LLM calls would crash the UI with raw tracebacks. Several call sites silently discarded errors or did nothing (`pass`).

**Key changes:**

- **`get_session()`**: wraps connection attempt; raises `ConnectionError` with actionable message. Module-level `Root(get_session())` catches this and calls `st.error()` + `st.stop()` instead of crashing.

- **`search_relevant_pages()` / `search_relevant_docstrings()` / `generate_chat_summary()`**: each now catches exceptions, logs them, and returns `None` — allowing the prompt to be built with whatever context succeeded (graceful degradation via `build_prompt`'s existing `if contents:` filter).

- **`build_question_prompt()`**: replaced `executor.map()` with `executor.submit()` + per-future `.result()` in a try/except, so one failing task doesn't kill the others:
  ```python
  for task_info, future in zip(task_infos, futures):
      try:
          context[task_info.name] = future.result()
      except Exception as e:
          logger.error(...)
          context[task_info.name] = None
  ```

- **`get_response()`**: catches LLM failures and raises `RuntimeError` with a user-facing message.

- **Main chat flow** (lines 483-521): wrapped in top-level `try/except` that shows `st.error()` instead of crashing.

- **`send_telemetry()`**: replaced silent `pass` with `logger.debug()`.

- **Feedback form**: replaced silent `pass` with `st.warning()` telling the user submission isn't implemented yet.

- **Bugfix**: rate-limit sleep used `time_diff.seconds + time_diff.microseconds * 0.001` (broken arithmetic mixing seconds and milliseconds); replaced with `time_diff.total_seconds()`.

author: sfwefr-ux
body:
## Problem
`vision_analyze` surfaces a hard error to the user on any transient failure from the vision backend. In practice this happens regularly with Gemini, which returns `HTTP 503 (UNAVAILABLE): "...currently experiencing high demand..."` during short load spikes that usually clear within seconds. A single 503 currently fails the whole image analysis.

## Fix
Wrap the vision LLM call in a bounded retry with capped exponential backoff:
- Retries transient failures only — HTTP 429/500/502/503/504 and overload/unavailable messages (detected via the exception's `status_code` and message text).
- Up to 4 attempts; delays 2 → 4 → 8s (capped at 15s).
- Non-transient errors (e.g. image-too-large / invalid request) are re-raised immediately, so the existing auto-resize and empty-content retry paths are untouched.

All three existing call sites (primary, post-resize, empty-content retry) route through the wrapper.

## Testing
- `py_compile` clean.
- Unit-level checks of the new helpers: transient classification (503/overload -> retry; 400/size -> no retry); retry-then-success (3 attempts, 2s/4s backoff); immediate re-raise of non-transient (no sleep); exhaustion after max attempts (2s/4s/8s backoff).

## Summary

First sprint of the Process & Task Mining MVP — the foundation on which every later mining feature builds. Greenfield: FastAPI + PostgreSQL backend, React+TS frontend, one-command Docker Compose. Implements backlog stories **1.3** (internal event-log data model), **1.1** (CSV import with mapping) and **5.1** (Docker deployment).

### Story 1.3 — Internal event-log data model & storage
Import-source-agnostic schema so all downstream mining reads from one model regardless of origin (CSV now; XES/DB adapters/Camunda later).

```
EventLog (id, name, source, imported_at, row_count, case_count)
  └─ Case (log_id, case_key)
       └─ Event (case_id, activity_id, resource_id?, timestamp, lifecycle?, cost?)
            └─ Attribute (event_id, key, value)   # extensible key-value
  ├─ Activity (log_id, name)   ├─ Resource (log_id, name)
```
Composite indexes `(log_id, timestamp)` and `(case_id, timestamp)` for query performance at scale; `ON DELETE CASCADE` for full-log deletion. Alembic autogenerated migration; SQLAlchemy 2.0 typed models.

### Story 1.1 — CSV import with column mapping
Two-step flow: `POST /api/logs/upload` streams the file to disk in 1 MB chunks (rejecting >500 MB) and returns a 20-row preview; `POST /api/logs/import` validates the mapping and ingests.

The mapping logic is pure/testable (no DB or HTTP):
```python
normalize_rows(rows, mapping) -> NormalizationReport(events, errors, skipped_rows)
# validation codes: missing_column, empty_case_id, empty_activity, unparseable_timestamp
```
Timestamps parsed via pandas with optional explicit `strftime`. `persist_log` deduplicates activities/resources/cases in-memory and bulk-inserts events in batches of 5000 for bounded memory on large logs. Frontend (`CsvImport.tsx`) guesses Case/Activity/Timestamp from headers, shows the preview table and a mapping form.

Unit tests cover 3 distinct CSV structures (comma, semicolon+cost, day-first dates) plus the full API flow.

### Story 5.1 — Docker Compose deployment
`docker compose up --build` starts `db` (postgres:16, healthcheck-gated), `backend` (entrypoint waits for DB → `alembic upgrade head` → uvicorn) and `frontend` (nginx serving the Vite build, proxying `/api` and `/health`). Secrets/ports via `.env` (see `.env.example`); no hardcoded credentials. `GET /health` reports API + DB status.

CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`): backend ruff + mypy + pytest, frontend lint + typecheck + build.

### Verification
Locally ran `docker compose up --build`, confirmed `/health` → `{"status":"ok","database":"ok"}`, frontend served on :3000, and a full upload→import→list→delete round-trip through the nginx proxy (sample at `samples/sample_log.csv`: 15 events / 4 cases / 5 activities). Backend: ruff, mypy, 15 pytest tests green. Frontend: lint, typecheck, build green.

## Summary

Adds a coherent `terminal.kitty-osc-live` admission/package slice for #1033: a SourceMeta/parser contract for line-framed Kitty OSC command observations, an EventContract for `shell.kitty/command.executed`, standard admission-policy acceptance, package-completeness coverage/debt/action refs, and regenerated source catalog/privacy coverage projections.

## Problem

Sinex already had typed Kitty command payload/canonicalizer support, but the Kitty OSC live mode was not represented as an accepted admission boundary: no source package metadata, parser manifest, EventContract, admission-policy reference, generated catalog/privacy projection, or package-gate coverage/debt/action refs connected the mode to the terminal activity package contract.

## Solution

- Add `KittyOscParser` under terminal source contracts for Unix-socket JSON frames carrying command, Kitty window/tab ids, optional sequence/cwd/exit/timing fields, and stream-frame material anchors.
- Register `event-contract:shell.kitty/command.executed@v1` with `terminal.kitty-osc-live` package refs and standard admission-policy acceptance.
- Preserve event identity when a frame omits `sequence` by adding a `sequence_or_frame` occurrence discriminator, and treat missing/invalid `timestamp_ns` as `StagedAtFallback` using acquisition time rather than pretending parse-time fallback is intrinsic.
- Extend package-completeness schema v2 with `coverage_debt_refs`, `operation_refs`, and runtime-binding `capabilities` surfaced from existing `SourceRuntimeBinding.capabilities`.

## Windows Port — Python Implementation

This PR adds a full-featured Windows port of Centered, reimplemented in Python using native Win32 APIs. All source files live in `CenteredWin/` alongside the existing macOS project.

### Features
- **Auto-center** on window focus, creation, and restore via `SetWinEventHook`
- **Cubic ease-out animation** — Instant, Subtle, and Smooth modes
- **Global hotkeys** — `Ctrl+Alt+C` (center active), `Ctrl+Shift+C` (center all), fully rebindable
- **Per-process exclusion list** — exclude apps by process name
- **Multi-display support** — follow the window's monitor or lock to a fixed display
- **Pause auto-centering** — toggle from the tray menu without losing manual hotkeys
- **Preferences UI** — Tkinter window for hotkeys, exclusions, display, and animation settings
- **Launch at Login** — managed via `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run`
- **Diagnostics** — copy settings summary to clipboard from the tray menu
- **JSON settings** — persisted in `%APPDATA%\CenteredWin\settings.json`

### Windows API Mapping

| macOS (Original) | Windows (This Port) |
|---|---|
| `AXUIElement` | `SetWindowPos` / `GetWindowRect` via `pywin32` |
| `AXObserver` | `SetWinEventHook` |
| `Carbon` global hotkeys | `RegisterHotKey` |
| `NSStatusItem` (menu bar) | `pystray` (system tray) |
| `UserDefaults` | JSON file in `%APPDATA%` |
| `SMAppService` (login item) | Registry `HKCU\...\Run` |

### Dependencies
```
pip install pywin32 pystray pillow psutil
```

### Running
```bash
pythonw CenteredWin/main.py
```

### Packaging as .exe
```bash
pip install pyinstaller
pyinstaller --noconsole --onefile CenteredWin/main.py
```

`actionlint` flagged 2 errors on `cross-env-deploy.yml`:

```
:36:21: property "build" is not defined in object type {deploy-dev: ...}
```

```diff
+    needs: [build, deploy-dev]
-    needs: deploy-staging
+    needs: [build, deploy-staging]
```
